en: I'm being let go at the end of this week.
Times are hard, after all.
Oh my, that is unfortunate.
But I know of no work I could find you.
No, of course not...
Starting tomorrow, I'll look for a new job.
Please put the book back when you're done.
...Sigh...
You said you were looking for work,
but it seems you work here.
Well, about that...
I'll keep on looking for work.
If you know of a good job, please tell me.
I've only got three days left to live.
note: Hyperbole: her job ends in 3 days (fired at the end of the week).

en: You mustn't say such things.
Surely there is plenty of work as a maid or nanny.
Without experience, nobody will hire me.
Before London, I helped out on a farm,
but that's no use here.
I tried the employment agency too, but
I just can't find a good job.
...What am I to do...
There were a few men at the agency, too.
I was surprised. It's hard for everyone.
I came to London without thinking...
But I'll keep looking a little longer.
At the agency I saw people who lean on
others and do nothing for themselves,
and I thought, I mustn't be like that.
I did think of going home
to work on the farm, but...
But, but,
I've found a new job now,
so I'll try a little longer.
Oh, is it about a job, by any chance?
Whatever do you mean?
I only came to pay my respects.
Oh... Ah, I'm sorry!
P-pardon me, I'm sorry. Goodbye.
I'm sorry about earlier.
I'm looking for work, you see...
After work I walked about job-hunting,
so I'm worn out today...
Sorry, please let me rest...
I'm doing well, thanks to you.
I've found a new job at last. I'm happy.
Cleaning, washing, I'll do anything!
Please come again!
Is there something I can do for you?
Oh dear... You're looking for work?
I can manage most things on my own.
Why not try somewhere else?
Oh, that's rather sudden.
I live alone, so I've no need of a nanny,
and I can do most things myself. Sorry.
May I take a book from the top shelf?
What's wrong? You look downcast.
I see... That's a shame.
I can't think of any job to offer you.
Starting tomorrow, I'll look for a new job.
Oh, it's you, Beth.
You said you were looking for work,
but you're working here, aren't you?
Even a not-so-good one would do...
note: Follows #10252 (msg 395141): 'If you know of a good job...' / 'Even a not-so-good one would do...'.

en: Don't lose heart. Keep at it.
Isn't there plenty of work as a maid or nanny?
What do you mean?
I'm sorry, just when you'd found a job.
But I, too,
had a job for you to do.
Not that it's a job only you
could do.
But you must do it for me, too.
Help me... won't you.
note: Player (gentle register), bite scene; no speaker tag in the message.

en: How long must I keep doing this?!
I'm the master's slave now,
so go on, give me any order you like.
Getting up of a morning's oddly hard.
...Too much drink, eh? Hah.
Give this old woman any order you please.
